options.counterfactual: Finite AW*-factors need not be monotone sequentially complete, so their defining assumptions alone do not guarantee a least upper bound for the sequence in the problem.
options.approach: Audit the asserted monotone sequential completeness theorem and distinguish it from completeness of the projection lattice and completeness in the quasitrace metric. Identify exactly which implication the proposed proof needs and whether it has been established.

options.approach: Start from a hypothetical witness and rigorously classify the increment changes obtainable by affine rescaling. Track the upper-bound set through the affine order isomorphism to preserve the absence of a least upper bound.

options.counterfactual: The attainable-increment set is empty even though finite AW*-factors can fail monotone sequential completeness; the fixed positive increment condition is the decisive obstruction.
options.approach: Use spectral cutoffs of the increments to obtain projections with uniformly positive quasitrace and bounded positive partial sums. Seek a projection-packing theorem strong enough to exclude such an infinite family.
